implementation: Verify real cgroup-v2 directory descriptors and each opened regular control file. Refuse symlinks and ordinary overmounted controls; open controls nonblocking so a substituted FIFO cannot hang before validation.
Prefer cgroup.kill. Only an absent or unsupported control permits the fallback; permission and read-only errors remain failures.

For the fallback, freeze and wait, pin process identities with pidfd_open, read current membership again, and signal only the pinned handles in bounded batches. Restore only a requested freezer state changed by this operation.
Read threaded-domain membership at the domain root; refuse independent cleanup of a populated threaded child.
Propagate stop failures through startup/shutdown sweeps and cleanup workers, preserving container files until a repaired cleanup succeeds.

local_verification.scope: Actual init tests: five unprivileged cgroup-stop checks, three filesystem-removal checks including failed-cleanup retry, and two PTY/process-table checks. Signals target only children created inside this owned container. No privileged cgroup mount, host PID churn, or complete engine replacement is exercised.
local_verification.compiler_failure_retained: The first build required an explicit io::Result<Process> annotation at the failed-spawn boundary; the corrected source builds for both Linux architectures.

previous_collector_correction.reason: Its same-line test-name/ok assertion rejected an expected diagnostic between the test name and the passing result.

collector.native_execution_reason: The control validation source changed; the ten unprivileged tests were run against the newly compiled binary.

required_hosted_cases.environment: ASAGIRI_REQUIRE_CGROUP_KILL_TEST=1 in the privileged disposable Linux unit-test job; absence of a writable cgroup-v2 mount fails the job.
cases: Modern nested cgroup.kill preserves a child outside the target subtree.
Forced pidfd fallback handles nested groups and more than one batch.
An already requested paused state is preserved.
A timeout restores the freezer without signaling retained processes.
Membership is read again after process handles are pinned and an owned child is moved.
Threaded-domain cleanup avoids unsupported child process-list reads.
Independent cleanup of a populated threaded child fails without freezing or signaling it.
Regular files over cgroup.kill/cgroup.procs and a FIFO over cgroup.procs are rejected without writes, blocked opens, or signals to retained children; every owned bind mount is removed.

remaining_limits: Real privileged cgroup cases, current-source platform checks and performance comparison have not run for this candidate.
No host PID churn, forced numeric PID reuse, or actual pre-cgroup.kill kernel runtime has been tested.
If pidfds are unavailable, the fallback fails and preserves files; it never reverts to numeric-PID signals.
Pidfds prevent signaling a recycled identity. A privileged external process migration after the membership check is not atomically excluded by the old-kernel fallback.
This work is not a formal proof of process lifecycle safety or the entire engine.
